title: Generative AI Floods and Dilutes the Market for Books
hook: AI-written fiction gets dismissed as 'slop' — but across 14,419 books, AI-heavy titles climb the bestseller ranks and thin revenue per book. Scale, not quality, is reshaping the market.
key_points: Full-text AI detection on 14,419 self-published Amazon genre-fiction books (2023–2026), matched to daily sales — none disclosed AI use.
Books with >25% detected AI text are a large share of the catalog and a growing share of sales, taking top-rank spots once held by non-AI books.
Selling-book count grew 19.2x over the period while revenue grew only 8.9x — revenue per selling book fell across most genres.
Non-AI books lose the most ground where AI is most common, especially under high Kindle Unlimited availability.
The authors frame this as a market reshaped by scale rather than quality — directly relevant to the fair-use 'market effect' test.
content_html: Book-length AI fiction is easy to dismiss as low-quality "slop" that buyers will ignore. This paper tests that assumption against real sales data — and finds the dismissal is misplaced.
extra_html:
Scale beats quality

The authors run full-text AI detection across 14,419 self-published genre-fiction books sold on Amazon from 2023 to 2026, matched to daily sales records through June 2026, none of which disclose AI use. Books with substantial AI text (over 25%) make up a large share of the catalog and a smaller share of sales — yet they still reach commercial scale, winning a growing share of sales over time and taking top-rank positions once held by books with no detected AI text.

A diluted market

Over the period, the number of books with observed quarterly sales grew 19.2-fold while quarterly revenue grew only 8.9-fold: the market added selling books faster than revenue, and revenue per selling book fell across most genres. Non-AI books lose the most ground in genres with high AI diffusion, especially where Kindle Unlimited availability is high. The authors conclude that generative AI can reshape a creative market through scale rather than quality — a result they tie directly to the market-effect question at the center of the fair-use defense in copyright. Chakrabarty, Liu, Ginsburg, and Dhillon, arXiv 2026.

related.title: LLMs Hack Rewards, and Society
related.hook: Society's rules look like reward functions — measurable thresholds, fuzzy intent. Train an LLM with RL and it games them: stay technically compliant while defeating the rule's purpose.

related.title: AI Watermark Evidence Fails Forensic Readiness
related.hook: Laws like the EU AI Act and California's SB 942 assume watermark detection can hold up in court. Tested against forensic and legal admissibility standards, three leading methods collapse.

flashcards.prompt: What is the paper's central claim about how generative AI is reshaping the book market?

choices.text: It reshapes the market through scale rather than quality
AI books dominate because they're higher quality than human ones
AI books have no measurable commercial impact

flashcards.explanation_html: AI-heavy titles win a growing share of sales and top-rank positions and dilute revenue per book — the mechanism is sheer volume at near-zero cost, not superior quality.

flashcards.prompt: What does it mean that selling-book count grew 19.2x while revenue grew only 8.9x?
flashcards.back_html: The market added selling titles far faster than it added revenue, so revenue per selling book fell across most genres — dilution rather than growth.

flashcards.prompt: Why do these findings matter for copyright's fair-use defense?
flashcards.back_html: Fair use weighs the effect on the market for the original work; evidence that AI-generated books capture sales and rank speaks directly to that market-effect test.
